q: The study examined several ____ in detail.
e: “children” is the correct plural form of “child.”

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “advice” correctly?
e: “advice” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: In British English, choose the sentence that treats “jury” as individual members.
o: The jury are divided in their opinions.
The jury are divided in its opinion.
The jury have divided in its opinions.
The jury is divided in its opinions.
e: A collective noun may take a plural verb in British English when its members act separately.

q: The study examined many ____ in detail.
e: “women” is the correct plural form of “woman.”

q: Choose the form showing that several drafts belong jointly to several writers.
e: A regular plural already ending in -s takes only an apostrophe for possession.

q: The study examined a few ____ in detail.
e: “criteria” is the correct plural form of “criterion.”

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “luggage” correctly?
e: “luggage” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “research” correctly?
e: “research” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: The study examined two ____ in detail.
e: “analyses” is the correct plural form of “analysis.”

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “information” correctly?
e: “information” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: The study examined three ____ in detail.
e: “phenomena” is the correct plural form of “phenomenon.”

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “equipment” correctly?
e: “equipment” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: Which sentence uses the uncountable noun “furniture” correctly?
e: “furniture” is normally uncountable and is not used with a/an or a regular plural ending.

q: Choose the correct possessive form: The letter belongs to Ali.
e: A singular proper noun normally forms the possessive with apostrophe + s.

q: The supervisor invited Sana and ____ to the office.
e: The pronoun is the object of “invited,” so the objective form “me” is required.

q: The candidate ____ application arrived first was interviewed today.
e: “Whose” is the relative possessive determiner modifying “application.”

q: Neither of the answers explains ____ clearly.
e: “Neither” is grammatically singular, so the reflexive pronoun is “itself.”

q: This is the researcher ____ discovered the error.
e: “Who” is the subject of the relative clause “who discovered the error.”

q: The blue folders are ours; the green ones are ____.
e: A possessive pronoun stands alone, so “theirs” is required.

q: The person to ____ Ali spoke was the director.
e: After the preposition “to,” formal grammar requires the objective relative pronoun “whom.”

q: Referring to Sara, complete the sentence: ____ and Ali completed the report.
e: A compound subject requires the subject form “he” or “she,” not an object, possessive, or reflexive form.

q: Ali prepared the entire letter by ____.
e: A reflexive pronoun must agree with its singular antecedent in person and gender.

q: During a trip organised by the clinic, Hira visited ____ Indus River.
e: Names of rivers normally take the definite article “the.”

q: At the garden, Noor was elected ____ chairperson of the committee.
e: An article is normally omitted after elect/appoint + unique official position.

q: In Iqra's class at the office, only ____ students understood the exceptionally difficult rule.
e: “A few” means some and is used with a plural countable noun.

q: After leaving the clinic, Iqra plays ____ chess to relax.
e: Names of games normally take no article when used generally.

q: For the course held at the office, Raza has read ____ book on the list.
e: “Every” is followed by a singular countable noun.

q: In the profile displayed at the clinic, Iqra is described as ____ MBA graduate.
e: The letter M is pronounced /em/, which begins with a vowel sound.

q: At the clinic, Ali warned that there was very ____ time left before the deadline.
e: “Little” is used with the uncountable noun “time” and stresses insufficiency.

q: In the profile displayed at the clinic, Sara is described as ____ hour-long interview.
e: “Hour” begins with a vowel sound because h is silent.

q: In the profile displayed at the office, Ali is described as ____ honest officer.
e: The initial h is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound.

q: At the office, the ____ child solved Noor's puzzle quickly.
e: An adjective is required before the noun “child.”

q: The instructions in Hira's letter for the museum were ____ enough for everyone to follow.
e: After the linking verb “were,” an adjective describes the subject “instructions.”

q: Choose the natural adjective order in Sana's sentence about the clinic: She bought a ____ table.
e: Opinion normally precedes size, and material comes close to the noun.

q: The news in Zara's letter made the students at the museum ____.
e: A complement after “made + object” describes the object and therefore takes an adjective.
